title: VitaBench
domain: Food delivery, in-store and travel requests from a simulated user, with up to 66 tools.
good_to_know: The paper's judge, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, is retired, so Like the paper cannot run: choose Any of your choice and a judge model. Scores compare only between runs with the same judge, never with the paper's.
Scores depend on the judge's and the simulated user's models: keep both fixed when comparing.
The leaderboard's main result is Cross-scenario, in Chinese, with 4 attempts per task.
A task passes only when every rubric is met.
upstream_limitations: In 15 of the 100 Cross-scenario (English) tasks, the shops, orders or bookings the task relies on are missing, though the Chinese version has them: an agent may fail them through no fault of its own. Score with the Chinese datasets.

Its model calls carry configuration fields (base_url, headers, name, max_input_tokens) that OpenAI's API refuses with HTTP 400: run every model of a VitaBench run on OpenRouter (OpenAI's models are there as openai/...) or a custom endpoint.
A failed model call makes the upstream start the conversation again, up to 3 times, and each costs its calls.
The updated leaderboard does not name its judge model.
Its dependencies are not locked to versions.
limitations: Another agent replaces the upstream's agent. It gets the upstream's prompt, plus lines from Nullius: where its tools are, and that its last message in a turn goes to the user.
With another agent, a judge that fails is the task's error: the upstream's restart of the conversation is not followed.
With another agent, one empty final message ends the conversation. The upstream asks its own agent 3 times.
There is no reference control: the upstream publishes no reference conversations.

datasets.title: VitaBench
datasets.verifier: VitaBench's evaluator: a judge model marks each task's rubrics.
